clue.text: Largely dishonest idiot from USA entering further presidential address?

indicators.note: the pieces go into the word for further, which then wraps around them
largely means most but not all, so the word for dishonest loses its last letter

parts.note: first half of MORE, meaning further
UNTRUE without its final letter
SHMO (or schmo) is American slang for a fool
second half of MORE, meaning further

explanation.surface: A jibe at a mostly crooked American fool giving yet another speech from the White House.
explanation.walkthrough: Shmo is US slang, so 'from USA' belongs to the idiot. The question mark flags the pun: the 'address' is a place, not a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Rushmore in South Dakota bears carved heads of four US presidents, so it is a location they jointly occupy, playfully called their address.

clue.text: Focus outside broadcast on hearing

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for an outside broadcast
a court sitting or hearing

explanation.surface: A TV crew filming outside a courtroom concentrates on the hearing inside.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece placed 'on' another sits above it, so OB comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is the single thing a mind is fixed upon, a noun synonym for a focus.

clue.text: Sign agreement to save space significantly

indicators.note: saving something means keeping it held safely inside, so one piece is kept within the other

parts.note: a nod is a sign of agreement
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: Signing a deal to save a great deal of room.
explanation.walkthrough: EN goes inside NOD. An en (like an em) is a printing measure of space, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverbial phrase 'no end' means hugely or a great deal, as in 'it helped no end'.

clue.text: Element of hillbilly language overheard

indicators.note: something overheard is caught by ear, so the words are judged by their sound rather than spelling

parts.note: a rube is an American country bumpkin, and an idiom is a form of language

explanation.surface: Someone catches a snatch of backwoods dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubidium is a soft alkali metal, a chemical element with atomic number 37.

clue.text: Puzzle party hosted by retired British/American

indicators.note: a host has the guest inside, so the party word sits within the others
retired means drawn back, so these abbreviations are read backwards

parts.note: abbreviation for the United States
abbreviation for the United Kingdom
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: A party thrown by a pensioner with dual British and American nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash keeps the two abbreviations as a pair, so the party can sit between them once the pair is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudoku is a number-placement logic game in a nine-by-nine grid, a kind of puzzle.

clue.text: Christian lyric-writer led by spirit, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word for spirit drops its last letter

parts.note: METHS, short for methylated spirits, minus its final letter
someone who writes odes, which are lyric poems

explanation.surface: A hymn writer guided mainly by the Holy Spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Meths is the British name for methylated spirits. In a down clue, being led by something puts that thing first.
explanation.definitionFit: A Methodist belongs to the Protestant denomination founded by John Wesley, so is one kind of Christian.

clue.text: Topless priest ruined weddings, perhaps

indicators.note: without its top, the word loses its first letter
something ruined has been wrecked, so its letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: priest without its first letter

explanation.surface: A disgraced cleric is said to have spoiled marriage ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding is one example of a religious ceremony, hence 'perhaps' marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Backing over University square

indicators.note: one word spread over another covers it on both sides, so it takes the other inside

parts.note: to be for something is to back it
standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Support for a college quadrangle.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside FOR. 'Backing' looks like a reversal signal but here it is the word for support.
explanation.definitionFit: Four is two multiplied by itself, so it is a square number.

clue.text: Passage of prose in Steinbeck shows genius

indicators.note: a passage is a short run of text, so the letters lie inside the stretch of words that follows

parts.note: the last letter of prose, then in, then the start of Steinbeck

explanation.surface: An excerpt of Steinbeck's writing proves he was brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein's name is used generically for a brilliant person, so it stands for any genius.

clue.text: Where you might get pearls reset, body having changed

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters of the two words are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A necklace is restrung after the wearer's figure has altered.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster bed is an area of seabed where oysters grow, and oysters produce pearls.

clue.text: I'm not impressed by technology backing everyone to score

parts.note: the tut of disapproval

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the abbreviation is read from right to left

parts.note: information technology

explanation.surface: Someone unmoved by the tech that helps every player compose music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To score' is part of the definition, placing it on a musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is the Italian direction written in a musical score telling all the performers to play together.

clue.text: Team in claret, say, was at home

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: first part of RED, as claret is a red wine
a side is a sports team
last letter of RED

explanation.surface: A football club in claret colours played at its home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: SIDE goes inside RED. Claret is a red Bordeaux wine; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to live in a place, so 'resided' is the past tense matching 'was at home'.

clue.text: Help child king to return ancient city

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the whole string is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the distress call
a son is a child
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A plea for a young prince to come back to his homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Knossos was the Bronze Age capital of Minoan Crete, a ruined city of antiquity.

clue.text: Rescues tortured soul in temptation

indicators.note: in places the jumbled word within the word for temptation
tortured means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: first part of BAIT, a lure or temptation
the letters of soul rearranged
last letter of BAIT

explanation.surface: Saving a tormented spirit that has fallen to temptation.
explanation.definitionFit: To bail someone out is an idiom for getting them out of trouble, so it means the same as saving them.

clue.text: Singer distressed by old band missing final note

indicators.note: the last letter of the band word is a musical note name, and it goes missing
distressed means battered or roughed up, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
band without its last letter, D, which is a note

explanation.surface: A vocalist upset at his former group for dropping the last note of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Dylan is the American singer-songwriter behind 'Blowin' in the Wind'.

clue.text: Planned redesign of cigarettes abandoned by one European

indicators.note: a redesign puts the parts together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
being abandoned by something means it leaves, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A European firm drops a scheduled repackaging of its cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: One E comes out of CIGARETTES, and the remaining nine letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Strategic describes something done according to a deliberate long-term plan, a close synonym for planned.

clue.text: Paper from Time magazine?

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a single edition of a magazine

explanation.surface: Asking whether some printed matter came from Time magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Time magazine pulls the two words together; split them to get the abbreviation and an edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is thin soft paper, as in tissue paper or a paper handkerchief.

clue.text: One powerful star mostly supported by a woman's love

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the word for star loses its last letter

parts.note: SUPERB, meaning star or first-rate, without its last letter
the possessive pronoun for a woman
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A mighty celebrity largely kept going by a woman's devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, being supported by something puts that thing underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A superhero is a fictional figure with superhuman abilities, literally someone with great power.

clue.text: Change line of footwear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to reverse one's position, a U-turn
second meaning: a type of rubber thong sandal

explanation.surface: A shoe company switching its range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' here means a product line, a kind of footwear rather than a row of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sudden reversal of opinion or policy and a simple sandal held on by a toe strap.

clue.text: Throw away a regrettably void type of code

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away
taken as written

indicators.note: something void is emptied, so only its shell of first and last letters remains

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Sadly discarding an empty kind of computer program.
explanation.walkthrough: To bin is everyday British for throwing in the rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Binary is the system of ones and zeros that underlies computer code.

clue.text: Some notes to hold down in confusion

parts.note: flats are notes lowered by a semitone
to pin is to hold down

explanation.surface: A pianist muddled about which keys to press.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a flat spin is an idiom for being in a state of panic or agitation, so it means bewildered.

clue.text: Encourage liberal nonsense

parts.note: to drive someone on is to urge them
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Someone urges a dismissal of left-wing rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivel is silly, worthless talk, a noun synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: Try each drunken sailor

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Questioning each of the drunken seamen one by one.
explanation.definitionFit: A yachter is someone who sails a yacht, hence a kind of sailor.

clue.text: Individual after carbon copy

indicators.note: coming after something means following it, so the word for individual is placed second

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
lone means single or individual

explanation.surface: A single person chasing a carbon copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Individual after carbon' puts the word for individual second. 'Carbon copy' reads as one phrase but splits into wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clone is an exact duplicate of something, so it is a copy.

clue.text: Cheek turned by stern religious adherent

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the word for cheek is read backwards

parts.note: lip is impudence or cheek
grim means stern

explanation.surface: A devout believer turns the other cheek to a forbidding person.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim travels to a holy place out of faith, so is a follower of a religion.

clue.text: Indian cloth I found under organ

parts.note: a lung is a body organ
taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of fabric discovered beneath a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, I found under the organ puts I at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A lungi is a cotton sarong wrapped round the waist, worn in India and South Asia.

clue.text: Writing possibly penned by top philosopher

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, as in a pen, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: first part of MAX, meaning the top or maximum
writing is one of the three Rs
last letter of MAX

explanation.surface: A text perhaps composed by a leading thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside MAX. The three Rs are reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic, so R can stand for any of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Marx was the German thinker who wrote Das Kapital, a political philosopher.

clue.text: Part of good restaurant recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
Noma is a famous Copenhagen restaurant

explanation.surface: A diner remembers a section of a fine eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: To be among a group is to be included in it, a preposition swapping for 'part of'.

clue.text: Breaking rule with one TV participant?

indicators.note: breaking something smashes it apart, so its letters can be reassembled in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A contestant on a television show flouts the regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is by example: someone who offers to take part.
explanation.definitionFit: A volunteer offers to take part in something of their own free will, so is a willing participant.

clue.text: Solver flying our helicopter

indicators.note: flying sends things up into the air to land anyhow, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone working out how to pilot the group's chopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solver' looks like a nod to the crossword solver, but it means a crime solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's Belgian detective, who solves murder cases.
